title: Upgrade Readiness Signal Oracle: lightweight preflight signal composer for LTS and rolling releases
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: build a small, composable 'Signal Oracle' that synthesizes multiple preflight checks into a single readiness score and recommendation for upgrade rollouts. The oracle will be the canonical source used by the rollout orchestrator to decide canary progression, abort criteria, and automatic rollback triggers for both rolling releases and LTS upgrade lanes.

Scope:
- Define a compact signal model (smokeSuccessRate, p95Delta, modelCompatibilityFailures, tokenizerDriftScore, kvCacheHitDelta, spikeErrors) that is cheap to compute in preflight and representative of production risk.
- Implement aggregator service that pulls existing smoke probes, perf probes, eval-suite verdicts, and compatibility prober outputs and reduces them into a timestamped readiness document.
- Provide JSON schema and a lightweight CLI to run the oracle locally in CI, and a small K8s job for nightly LTS preflight runs.
- Wire oracle output to rollout orchestration: mapped to canary thresholds, abort reasons, and human-readable evidence links.

Non-goals: full rewrite of existing evals or new long-running e2e tests. This is a synthesis layer over current probes and small additional probes for tokenizer drift and KV cache smoke checks.
acceptance_criteria: Oracle produces a readiness JSON for a candidate runtime build with all signal fields populated
Rollout orchestrator can consume oracle output and make a deterministic canary decision in the staging pipeline
Local CLI reproduces CI run and returns identical readiness result for same inputs
Nightly LTS job emits readiness history to the release dashboard and alerts if readiness score drops below 0.7
Benchmarks: oracle end-to-end evaluation completes within 3 minutes in CI for a standard candidate build
implementation_steps: Design signal schema and scoring rules (mapping raw probes to normalized 0..1 sub-scores)
Add two lightweight probes: tokenizer drift check (sample prompt set, tokenization difference rate) and KV cache smoke (cache miss/regression checker)
Aggregator service: implement fetchers for smoke probes, perf harness (p95/p99), eval verdicts, compatibility prober outputs; normalize and score
CLI and CI job: containerize aggregator and add a pipeline step in preflight-runner; ensure reproducible inputs via pinned artifact manifests
Dashboard integration: post readiness document to /release-dashboard/api/preflight and add visualization in Console (QA: per-route/ model breakdown)
Rollout wiring: add mapping table in orchestrator -> canary decision matrix, add abort reason parsing and human links to evidence
Run cross-team validation: invite PMs, SRE, and Runtime team for review; run LTS nightly and iterate thresholds based on historical runs
decisions: Normalized scoring range 0..1 per signal with geometric mean aggregator to avoid single high score masking multiple low-risk signals
Threshold default 0.75 for automated canary progression; 0.90 recommended for LTS promotion; thresholds configurable by release lane
Tokenization drift probe is sampled and limited to 1k prompt checks per run to keep compute cost low
Oracle runs as a separate short-lived k8s Job to reduce blast radius and simplify RBAC rather than embedding inside the orchestrator pod
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy perf signals may flip readiness frequently -> Mitigation: use rolling-window smoothing and require consecutive failing runs (2) before abort
Risk: false positives from tokenizer drift on unusual prompt sets -> Mitigation: maintain curated prompt corpus per major model family and weight drift accordingly
Risk: aggregator becomes single point of failure in pipeline -> Mitigation: make step non-blocking in initial rollout (warn-only) and require manual approval for LTS until 3 successful runs

notes: This ticket intentionally keeps the oracle lightweight. The long-term plan is to evolve the signal set as we onboard more eval suites (semantic-accuracy, hallucination metrics) but keep the oracle fast for preflight usage. The scoring rules should be fully auditable and stored in repo as YAML so release engineers can tune without code changes.
